newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Toolex sees no market recovery yet.
newsitem.headline: Toolex sees no market recovery yet.

text.p: Optical discs equipment maker Toolex-Alpha NV said on Tuesday that its difficult market situation has not yet shown any signs of reviving.

"Trading in 1997 has yet to show any recovery from the depressed situation in the second half of 1996, and current backlog and order visibility is weak," chief executive Goran Barsby said in a statement.

But Barsby noted that the music industry has recently expressed confidence that markets will recover in the second half of 1997, which together with increased adoption of the CD-R and DVD technologies should lead to improved market conditions.

Earlier Toolex, which is Stockholm-based but whose shares are listed in Amsterdam and on NASDAQ, reported its 1996 net income had fallen to 76.2 million Swedish crowns from 90.4 million in the previous year.

The company said the slowdown in revenue growth of the music industry, which currently represents about 77 percent of all CDs that are shipped, depressed revenues in the second half of 1996 in particular.
In the world's top-10 markets, the value of audio sales is expected to have shown no real growth last year, it added.

Moreover, estimates published in late 1996 suggest that global CD production capacity continued to increase substantially in 1996 although the rate of growth was significantly lower than expected, Toolex-Alpha said.

But the company said the slowdown in growth rates were not uniform throughout the world, and the Asian markets in particular remained buoyant as evidenced by Toolex-Alpha's 65 percent growth in sales in that region.
